newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH-Costello sees 1996 easings delivering growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH-Costello sees 1996 easings delivering growth.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello told parliament today that the 1996 monetary easings would deliver the growth that he has forecast.
If we take his statement at face value, it implies that no further easing is needed to deliver those forecasts.
Unfortunately, he said this in a fabulously long, 123-word sentence that almost completely buried the message.
The argument for another easing is that inflation is low, the inflationary outlook is favourable and the economy is currently soft.

The argument against an easing is that the economy, soft as it may be now, will be fine later in the year -- as the government's mid-year review forecast last week with its projection of 3.5 percent GDP growth in 1996/97.

Costello appears to have said that, thanks to last year's easings (which together with bank discounting are worth A$188 a month to an average home borrower), the economy will be fine later in the year.
We present the full quote below, but patient readers will be better off if they first read this simplified reconstruction of what Costello said:

--As a result of the 1996 rate cuts, which some banks have only just passed on, and considering the family tax break that the government has implemented, we will see the strong and solid growth forecast in last week's mid-year review.
If you've digested that, here's the original:

--"As a result of those interest rate reductions coming on stream, some which were only passed on in the last week by some of the banks -- and I've already expressed to the House my own view that banks ought to be passing onto home buyers reductions in official interest rates with the same alacrity that they pass on the rises in official rates -- some of those only coming to the benefit in the last week but giving that benefit of A$188 per month over future months, putting back disposable income into the hands of Australian families, together with the family policy that the prime minister has already indicated, providing through the year strong and solid growth as forecast in the mid-yea
